title: Ask the class, copy the notes
allegory: An attention head is a pupil in a classroom of notebooks: it asks a question, every pupil sitting earlier holds up a label, the best matches fly their notes over by paper plane, and the pupil adds a summary of those notes into its own notebook.
map: the question the current pupil asks
the label each earlier pupil holds up
how well each label fits the question, turned into shares that add up to 1
the attention pattern: softmax(q·k / √d_head) over earlier positions only
the notes flown over and written into your own notebook
values weighted by the pattern, mapped through W_O and added to the stream
credit: Query, key and value as 'what am I looking for', 'what do I contain' and 'what I will communicate' is Andrej Karpathy's framing, from 'Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out'.
where_else: Induction heads: a learned attention pattern that finds an earlier copy of the current token and reads what came next
KV caching: past keys and values never change, so they are stored and reused
Bahdanau, Cho and Bengio's translation model, where the decoder soft-searches every source word
Any soft lookup: match a query against keys, then take a weighted read of the values

hamming.what: The unit that moves information between positions: each position asks a question, matches it against earlier positions' labels and copies a blend of their contents.
hamming.when: In every layer of every transformer, and whenever you want to know which earlier tokens influenced the current one.
hamming.why: It is the only part of a transformer that moves information across positions (the MLPs work within one position), so circuits like induction heads live here.

object.title: The note-passing grid
object.subtitle: Each row is one pupil sharing out one full unit of attention over the seats it is allowed to see.

knobs.label: Which earlier seat it looks for

cap.1: Each row is one pupil deciding whose notes to copy. Its towers add up to one full share, and nothing stands above the diagonal: no peeking ahead.
cap.2: Rows are queries, columns are keys, height is attention weight. Each row sums to 1, and the upper triangle is masked.
cap.3: The pattern is softmax over key_pos of q·k/√d_head, with −inf added where key_pos > query_pos.

cap.1: Sharpen the question and each pupil copies almost entirely from the seat just before it. That is a previous-token head.
cap.2: Large score gaps make softmax nearly one-hot: each position reads almost only from position t − 1.
cap.3: Scaling the logits sharpens the softmax toward an argmax; a previous-token head concentrates mass on key t − 1.

cap.1: A vague question spreads the share evenly over everyone visible. Early pupils have few neighbours, so each gets a bigger slice.
cap.2: With flat scores the pattern is uniform over visible keys: row t gives each earlier position 1/(t+1).
cap.3: Zero logit differences give a uniform distribution over the unmasked prefix, so the head averages the values it can see.

cap.1: Change what the question looks for and the ridge moves. Now each pupil mostly reads its own notebook.
cap.2: Different W_Q and W_K learn different matching rules; here the peak sits on the diagonal (attend to self).
cap.3: The QK circuit alone decides where mass goes; changing it moves the ridge without touching what gets copied.

cap.1: Look three seats back. The first pupils can't, so their share piles onto the earliest seat they can see.
cap.2: Early rows have fewer visible keys, so their mass lands on the closest allowed position.
cap.3: Near the start of the sequence the mask truncates the support, so the softmax puts the mass on the nearest allowed key.

predict.q: Why are there no towers above the diagonal?

options.t: The causal mask: a position may not read later positions
Those weights just happened to be learned as zero

predict.why: Scores for later keys are set to −inf before the softmax, so they get exactly zero share.

predict.q: Why mask the scores to −inf instead of zeroing the probabilities after the softmax?

options.t: So each row still sums to 1
It is faster on a GPU

predict.why: Zeroing after the softmax leaves rows summing to less than 1, silently shrinking the head's output, worst at early positions.

predict.q: The query-key match decides where to look. What decides what gets copied?
predict.why: QK picks the positions; W_V and then W_O decide what information moves and where it is written in the stream.

object.where: Any soft lookup: a query matched against keys, then a weighted read of values, as in KV caches and retrieval.
